## What it will cover

::: {.mm-stub-outline}
- The QSAR workflow from assay data to model
- Scaffold splits and time splits versus random splits
- Applicability domain: when not to trust a prediction
- Uncertainty estimates with ensembles and conformal methods
- Activity cliffs and near-duplicates as leakage
- Lab 6: a scaffold-split benchmark on a MoleculeNet dataset
:::

## Planned learning outcomes

1. Build a QSAR model with a scaffold split and explain why its score differs from a random split.
2. Estimate an applicability domain and flag out-of-domain predictions.
3. Attach calibrated uncertainty to property predictions and communicate it to a chemist.

## In the meantime

Everything here builds on Part I, in particular the evaluation habits of [Chapter 2](../../part-1-foundations/ch02-ml-fundamentals/index.html). Episode [2.6](../../part-1-foundations/ch02-ml-fundamentals/06-pipelines-leakage.html) already introduces the group splits that become scaffold splits here.
